title: Moses older than the Greek sages; day one
english: Clement, Africanus, and Tatian — and from those of the circumcision Josephus and Justus — each told, from old history in his own way, that the inspired Moses flourished in the time of Inachus. Inachus stands seven hundred years before the Trojan war. One of the saints, making a most careful reckoning of the times against the years of Inachus, found the most holy Jacob a contemporary; Moses he found with Josephus. For inventing a parallel chronicle, he set beside each other the ruler in every nation, and gathered the years of the kingdoms of the Chaldeans, Assyrians, Medes, Persians, Lydians, Hebrews, Egyptians, Athenians, Argives, Sicyonians, Lacedaemonians, Corinthians, Thessalians, Macedonians, Latins — later called Romans — and […] the years of each nation’s kings, setting Abraham’s years against those of the Assyrian queen Semiramis. For under Semiramis the blessed Abraham was known; Josephus places him under Inachus; Moses under Cecrops, whom the children of the Greeks [call] first of Attica three hundred years before the Trojan affairs — so that Moses is oldest among the ancient sages of the Greeks, earlier than Homer and Hesiod and the Trojan matters, than Heracles, Musaeus, Linus, Chiron, Orpheus, the Dioscuri, Asclepius, Dionysus, Hermes, Apollo, and the Greek mysteries and rites and even the deeds of Zeus; earlier too than Deucalion’s flood, Phaethon’s burning, Erichthonius born of Hephaestus and earth, and the rape of Kore. For all these came after Cecrops, whom Homer and Hesiod fall far short of in years. And if they are younger than these, they are much lower still than Moses’ age. So Moses was shown the most divine teacher of truth among all the wise. Spitting out what is called Egyptian wisdom, he spoke best of this world’s framing — clearly inspired with the truth by the God over all, the Maker of the whole. For he says: [[In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth >> Bible:Genesis 1:1]]. And many among the Greeks who dared to teach the opposite were sunk into a deep of ignorance. Doctrines put forward from human thought are […] and without ballast. Among them no word stands unmoved — the later always overthrowing the earlier — so the faithful need not labor to refute them; they suffice for one another’s overturning. What shape and substance heaven is, Isaiah teaches us, saying: [[He who set the heaven as a vault >> Bible:Isaiah 40:22]] — hinting it is thin, not solid or thick — as elsewhere: [[He who established the heaven as smoke >> Bible:Isaiah 51:6]]. And the psalm says the earth is fixed on the waters: [[He founded it upon the seas, and prepared it upon the rivers >> Bible:Psalm 24:2]]. And how this is we must not pry into, but believe. For the simplicity of faith is stronger than reasoned proofs; God’s judgments are unreachable and incomprehensible. So on the first day God made the heaven and the earth and the light, and in a sharp turn of time lit everything — and this light is the corruptible one. Before it, a dark shadowing held things when heaven was stretched round and made the leftover place lightless. Outside heaven there is unshadowed, incorruptible, eternal light in which angels dwell, of which Solomon says: [[Light for the righteous forever >> Bible:Proverbs 13:9]] — into which those who have lived well also take their rest. You will grasp this…
